summary: Proposal Phase 2, Task 2d-1 — the engagement-letter signing rule ('all' = every required signatory signed / 'any' = at least one) becomes ONE callable function, public.el_signature_progress(uuid) -> jsonb, and lifecycle_onboarding_gates is re-issued to call it instead of re-implementing it inline. Also widens engagement_letters_status_check with 'partially_signed'. NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: the re-issued gate is byte-identical to the live body (def-hash 6f60145c17a3f46b894ef8807005012a, shipped by 20260727130000_split_onboarding_gate.sql) except that the inline rule block is replaced by the call; the rule's semantics are preserved exactly (has_signatories mirrors the previous EXISTS(required rows) branch test; satisfied computes the same 'any' => signed >= 1 / 'all' => total > 0 AND signed = total over the same rows). The status widening is additive — every previously allowed value is still allowed, and nothing writes the new value until Task 2d-2.

problem.context: T2b (20260727130000) put the signature rule INLINE inside lifecycle_onboarding_gates. Task 2d-2 adds the writer side — the per-signatory signing RPC — which must evaluate exactly the same rule to decide 'partially_signed' vs 'signed'. Two copies of a load-bearing rule in two SECURITY DEFINER functions is the vocabulary/logic drift this codebase has repeatedly been bitten by, so the rule is extracted to a single function BEFORE the second caller exists. The 'partially_signed' token lands on engagement_letters.status (a display projection of the signatory rows, which stay the source of truth) — NOT on quotes.status, per the resolved decision that partial signing is a post-acceptance signing state.
problem.scope: One new function; one re-issued function (gate); one widened CHECK. lifecycle_approve_onboarding, lifecycle_evaluate_onboarding_activation, every signing RPC, every RLS policy and all table data are untouched.

live_bodies_used.basis: Live hash equals the body this repo shipped in supabase/migrations/20260727130000_split_onboarding_gate.sql (recorded as the post-apply hash of that release and re-confirmed live via catalog_functions before authoring this migration), so the re-issue is based on the exact live body, not a transcription.

expected_objects.object: function public.el_signature_progress(uuid) returns jsonb, STABLE, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path=public
expected_objects.verify_via: catalog_functions(name_like: 'el_signature_progress') -> expect exactly one row, volatility 'stable', security_definer true, search_path 'search_path=public'. Record its def-hash in .livebodies/README.md.

expected_objects.object: public.lifecycle_onboarding_gates(uuid) re-issued to call el_signature_progress; still STABLE SECURITY DEFINER and still returning activation_ready
expected_objects.verify_via: catalog_functions(name_like: 'lifecycle_onboarding_gates', include_source: true) -> def-hash CHANGED from 6f60145c17a3f46b894ef8807005012a; body contains 'public.el_signature_progress(v_letter_id)' and contains NO 'v_sig_rule'/'v_req_total'/'v_req_signed'; still contains the activation_ready computation excluding billing. Then db_rpc lifecycle_onboarding_gates on any application id and confirm the returned key set is unchanged (gates/all_pass/activation_ready/billing_settled/outstanding).

expected_objects.object: CHECK engagement_letters_status_check allows draft, sent, partially_signed, signed — and is the ONLY check constraint on engagement_letters.status
expected_objects.verify_via: Confirm the migration's NOTICE named the replaced constraint (expected 'engagement_letters_status_check'). Then verify the live constraint definition lists all four values and that no second check constraint on the status column remains.

rollback.assessment: Low risk, forward-only. The gate can be restored by re-applying 20260727130000_split_onboarding_gate.sql section (A) verbatim; el_signature_progress would then be an unused function. The CHECK can be narrowed again only while no row stores 'partially_signed' (nothing writes it until Task 2d-2).
rollback.data_risk: None. No table data is read or written by this migration; the CHECK is widened, so no existing row can be invalidated.

steps: Apply migration 20260727140000_el_signature_rule_sot.sql via the Lovable migration flow.
Confirm the card returns green AND a row exists in supabase_migrations.schema_migrations (verify against LIVE, not just Test).
In the live app, open an onboarding application and confirm its gate/approval behaviour is unchanged (this migration must change nothing a user can see).
After apply: refresh docs/audits/unapplied-migrations-baseline.json with the new applied version so the drift guard stays green.
Notify Claude to run the expected-object verification and complete this receipt (move out of pending/).

post_apply_followups: Task 2d-2: public per-signatory signing RPC (own token per signatory) that records the signature, calls el_signature_progress, sets engagement_letters.status to 'partially_signed' or 'signed', and — on satisfaction — writes onboarding_applications.contracts_signed_at (the drift defect in public_sign_engagement_letter_by_token, live def-hash 79c37859dcfbe37a56a3314f03c04f1c, which today sets none of it).

Task 2d-3: seed engagement_letter_signatories from quotes.signatory_snapshot at engagement-letter dispatch and email each signatory their own link (send-engagement-letter currently sends one email to onboarding_applications.email using the letter-level signature_token); signing page resolves either token.
